localNote: Glasgow's three Wetherspoons pubs occupy some of the city's most impressive buildings. The Counting House on George Square is a grand former Bank of Scotland headquarters, The Crystal Palace on Jamaica Street has a striking Victorian cast-iron frame, and Hengler's Circus on Sauchiehall Street stands on the site of a beloved entertainment venue.

pubs.name: The Counting House
pubs.history: A Category A listed building designed by J.T. Rochead between 1867 and 1870 in the Italian Renaissance style. It served as the Bank of Scotland's Glasgow headquarters for over a century. Wetherspoon's first pub in Scotland, opened in 1996. The original bank vaults are used as a seating area.
pubs.nearestStation: Glasgow Queen Street station, about 3 minutes on foot

pubs.name: The Crystal Palace
pubs.history: Built in 1855 by architect John Baird, inspired by Joseph Paxton's Crystal Palace from the 1851 Great Exhibition. The cast-iron frame and over a hundred arched windows create a distinctive greenhouse effect. The building originally served as a furniture warehouse and retains a Victorian cast-iron lift.
pubs.nearestStation: Glasgow Central station, about 5 minutes on foot

pubs.name: Hengler's Circus
pubs.history: Named after the circus that occupied the site from 1904 to 1924. Before that the building hosted a diorama, a panorama and an ice rink. Wetherspoon took over in 2001. The interior celebrates the site's long history as a popular entertainment venue.
pubs.nearestStation: Buchanan Street subway station, about 5 minutes on foot
